title: European shares hold gains ahead of events blizzard
text:
Shutterstock photo UPDATE 1-European shares hold gains ahead of events blizzard
* FTSE 100 rallies ahead of Brexit vote
* Results boost Sartorius
* Wall Street trades cautiously
By Josephine Mason
LONDON, Jan 29 (Reuters) - European shares closed higherahead of a blizzard of political, economic and corporate events,with a Brexit vote and Apple results on Tuesday and a FederalReserve decision and Sino-U.S. trade talks on Wednesday.
The pan-European STOXX 600 .STOXX index ended the day up0.8 percent, while London's FTSE 100 .FTSE rallied by morethan 1.3 percent ahead of the vote in Parliament on Brexit.
Gains were spread among most sectors and bourses but Investors shunned stocks or indexes exposed to U.S.-China trade,such as Frankfurt's DAX GDAXI , which limited its gains to 0.1percent or automotives .SXAP , which fell 0.5 percent.
News that the United States levelled criminal chargesagainst China'sHuaweiHWT.UL before the new round of talksbetween Washington and Beijing added to the subdued mood.
Trading was limited with FTSE 100 turnover at 88 percent ofthe average 90 day daily volume, STOXX 600 at 85 percent and DAXat 77 percent.
The mood was however better in Europe than on Wall Streetwhere indexes were slightly in the red.
Stéphane Barbier de la Serre, a strategist at Makor CapitalMarkets, said European markets had catching up to do and thatWednesday's U.S. monetary meeting was making investors theremore cautious.
"Let's wait for the Fed", summed up their thinking, he said.
The European technology sector .SX8P , down 0.5 percent, was also among the few losers with SAP SAPG.DE , Europe's mostvaluable technology company, down 2.7 percent after its results.
Technology stocks in the U.S. were also retreating withApple AAPL.O set to report after market close and Amazon.comAMZN.O , Facebook FB.O and MicrosoftMSFT.O , all scheduledto report later this week.
Among individual moves, Germany's Sartorius SATG.DE jumped18.2 percent after its results.
Royal MailRMG.L hit an all-time lows after failing todeliver its full-year results.
Shares in Scor SCOR.PA sank 11.4 percent. The Frenchreinsurer is suing rival Covea and its chief executive forbreach of trust after Covea announced it had abandoned plans fora friendly takeover of Scor. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL5N1ZT3OO (Reporting by Josephine Mason, Julien Ponthus and Marc Jones,editing by Danilo Masoni/Angus MacSwan/Alexander Smith) ((mailto: Josephine.Mason@thomsonreuters.com ; +44 207 542 7695;Reuters Messaging:rm:// josephine.mason.reuters.com@reuters.net ))
